Moses says, “This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.” (Deuteronomy 20:15) So the offer of peace, and what follows it, is for those faraway cities. Then verse 16 switches to the cities of the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance, and that's a different command.

It's actually True, friend. Moses says, “This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.” (Deuteronomy 20:15) The peace offer and what comes after it belong to those faraway cities. Verse 16 then gives a different command, for the cities of the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance.

Yes, send that man home! The officers ask, “Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him return home…” (Deuteronomy 20:5) Picture him out there with a brand new house he's never even dedicated. I think his mind is back at that front door the whole time. If he falls in battle, they say, “…another man dedicate it.” (Deuteronomy 20:5)

Yes, commanders. The text says, “When the officers have finished addressing the army, they are to appoint commanders to lead it.” (Deuteronomy 20:9) The priest had his say, the officers had their say, and THEN somebody gets put in charge. That's a lot of talking before anybody takes the lead, and I know a thing or two about waiting around for my turn.

Yes. The text says, “If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.” (Deuteronomy 20:11) The offer of peace comes first in verse 10, and accepting it is the road that skips the siege. I think this is a heavy part of the passage, so we won't joke around here.

That's right, baker! Moses says, “But if they refuse to make peace with you and wage war against you, lay siege to that city.” (Deuteronomy 20:12) Think about what has to happen for that siege to even start. The city heard the offer of peace from verse 10 and said no, and then it waged war on top of that. That's the city that gets a siege.
